traceability.evidence:
Key evidence confirming full implementation of docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md:
1) Core maintenance API implementation - src/maintenance/index.ts - Exports the full maintenance surface: - detectStaleAnnotations - updateAnnotationReferences - batchUpdateAnnotations - verifyAnnotations - generateMaintenanceReport - JSDoc annotated with @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and all REQ-MAINT-* IDs (REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE).
- src/maintenance/detect.ts (REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE) - detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - Resolves a workspace root from process.cwd() + codebasePath. - If root does not exist or is not a directory, returns [] (safe no-op). - Uses getAllFiles(workspaceRoot) to traverse only existing directories. - Reads each file and scans with regex /@story\s+([^\s]+)/g. - For each story path: - Skips unsafe paths using isUnsafeStoryPath (prevents traversal/absolute/invalid-extension checks). - Resolves project and workspace candidates and enforces project boundary via enforceProjectBoundary. - Only checks fs.existsSync on in-project candidates. - If none exist, adds the original story path to a Set of stale annotations. - Returns Array.from(stale) for de-duplicated stale @story paths. - Includes branch-level @story/@req/@supports annotations explicitly tying behavior to REQ-MAINT-DETECT and REQ-MAINT-SAFE (e.g., handling boundary enforcement failures as out-of-project and skipping unsafe paths).
- src/maintenance/update.ts (REQ-MAINT-UPDATE) - updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath): number - Validates that codebasePath exists and is a directory; otherwise returns 0 (safe no-op). - Uses getAllFiles(codebasePath) to traverse files. - Escapes oldPath for regex and builds pattern `(@story\s*)${escapedOldPath}`. - For each file, processFileForAnnotationUpdates reads content and performs a replace with callback that: - Increments replacementCountRef.count - Returns `${p1}${newPath}` (preserving @story prefix and whitespace; only path part changes). - Writes file back only if newContent !== content, preserving formatting otherwise. - Returns total replacement count. - Fully covers the requirement to update annotation references when story files are moved/renamed while preserving code/formatting.
- src/maintenance/batch.ts (REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY) - batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings: {oldPath,newPath}[]): number - Loops over mappings, summing results of updateAnnotationReferences for each mapping. - Implements batch updates across multiple files and annotations. - verifyAnnotations(codebasePath): boolean - Calls detectStaleAnnotations and returns true if the resulting array is empty. - Verifies annotations after maintenance operations.
- src/maintenance/report.ts (REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE) - generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string - Calls detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath). - If no stale annotations, returns "" (explicitly signaling no work needed: safe behavior). - If there are stale annotations, returns newline-separated list of stale story paths. - This is a programmatic basis for the reporting requirement.
- src/maintenance/utils.ts - getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] - Validates dir exists and is a directory; returns [] otherwise. - Recursively traverses the directory with traverseDirectory, collecting only regular files. - This underpins workspace-wide maintenance operations, consistent with story expectations.
2) CLI implementation and UX (traceability-maint) - package.json - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } - Exposes maintenance tools via a CLI binary, as required by the story.
- src/maintenance/cli.ts (REQ-MAINT-DETECT/VERIFY/REPORT/UPDATE/BATCH/SAFE) - Exports runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv: string[]): number. - Uses normalizeCliArgs from src/maintenance/flags.ts to parse subcommand and args. - Behavior: - When no subcommand or when -h/--help is provided: - Calls printHelp(), printing usage text with commands and options. - Returns EXIT_OK (0). - Otherwise, uses a switch(command): - "detect" -> handleDetect - "verify" -> handleVerify - "report" -> handleReport - "update" -> handleUpdate, with additional help printing when EXIT_USAGE is returned. - default -> prints "Unknown command: ", prints help, returns EXIT_USAGE. - Wrapped in try/catch: - On unexpected errors, logs `traceability-maint failed: ` to stderr and returns EXIT_USAGE. - At EOF, if require.main === module, it calls process.exit(runMaintenanceCli(process.argv)), making it truly executable as a CLI.
- src/maintenance/commands.ts (REQ-MAINT-DETECT/VERIFY/REPORT/UPDATE/SAVE) - Provides subcommand handlers wired to the maintenance API: - EXIT_OK = 0, EXIT_STALE = 1, EXIT_USAGE = 2.
- handleDetect(normalized) - Parses flags (parseFlags) to get root and json. - Calls detectStaleAnnotations(root) -> stale. - If json flag: - console.log(JSON.stringify({ root, stale })). - Else if stale.length === 0: - console.log("No stale @story annotations found."). - Else: - Prints each stale path and a summary line including guidance to run report. - Returns EXIT_OK if stale.length === 0 else EXIT_STALE. - Implements detection UX and clear feedback.
- handleVerify(normalized) - Parses flags; calls verifyAnnotations(root) -> boolean. - If valid, prints `All traceability annotations under ${root} are valid.` and returns EXIT_OK. - Otherwise, prints a guidance message referring to detect/report and returns EXIT_STALE.
- handleReport(normalized) - Parses flags; supports format text|json with default text. - Calls generateMaintenanceReport(root) -> string. - If format === "json": outputs JSON { root, report }. - Else if report is empty: prints "No stale @story annotations found. Nothing to report.". - Else: prints a small Markdown-like report including root and the stale references. - Always returns EXIT_OK when arguments are valid.
- handleUpdate(normalized) - Parses flags; root, from, to, json, dryRun. - If !from or !to: - console.error("'update' requires --from and --to ."); - Returns EXIT_USAGE. - If dryRun: - Uses generateMaintenanceReport(root) to estimate stale count. - If json: logs JSON with mode: "dry-run", root, from, to, estimatedStaleCount. - Else prints: "Dry run: no files were modified.", followed by explanation of what would be updated and estimated count. - Returns EXIT_OK. - Else (real update): - const count = updateAnnotationReferences(root, from, to). - If json: logs JSON { root, from, to, updated: count }. - Else prints: `Updated ${count} @story annotation(s) from '${from}' to '${to}' under ${root}.`. - Returns EXIT_OK. - Enforces safe usage (REQ-MAINT-SAFE) and provides clear feedback on what was changed or would be changed.
- src/maintenance/flags.ts (REQ-MAINT-SAFE) - Implements ParsedCliInput, NormalizedCliArgs, ParsedFlags. - parseCliInput(argv) splits out node, script, subcommand, args. - normalizeCliArgs uses parseCliInput and returns { subcommand, args }. - parseFlags(normalized) constructs ParsedFlags with defaults (root = process.cwd(), json = false) via createDefaultFlags. - Recognizes and safely handles: - --root (resolves via path.resolve) - --json - --format (throws error for other values -> CLI catch leads to EXIT_USAGE and error message) - --from, --to - --dry-run - applyFlag orchestrates each handler; unrecognized args are ignored (safe, minimal parsing).
3) Tests validating each requirement - All tests run and pass - Command executed: `npm test -- --verbose` - Jest output shows all maintenance-related tests passing: - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - tests/maintenance/index.test.ts - tests/perf/maintenance-large-workspace.test.ts - tests/perf/maintenance-cli-large-workspace.test.ts - Summary: Test Suites: 1 skipped, 48 passed, 48 of 49 total; Tests: 2 skipped, 371 passed, 373 total; no failures associated with Story 009.0.
- tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts (explicitly references docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md) - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect exits with code 0 and message when no stale annotations. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits with code 0 when annotations valid (temp workspace with matching story file). - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits with code 1 and prints guidance when annotations are stale or invalid. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] report prints human-readable summary including "Traceability Maintenance Report" and the stale story path. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] report prints "No stale @story annotations found. Nothing to report." when no stale annotations exist. - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] update performs replacements of @story old.path.md -> new.path.md and exits 0. - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] update without --from/--to returns exit code 2 and emits an error plus help. - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] dry-run does not modify files and exits 0. - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] report with `--format yaml` returns exit code 2, error message includes "Invalid format: yaml" and "Expected 'text' or 'json'". - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect with --json returns exit code 1 and prints JSON with stale array containing expected story. - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect with non-existent --root exits 0 and prints "No stale @story annotations found.". - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] no subcommand prints help and exits 0 with no errors. - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] permission error simulation via fs.statSync throwing EACCES causes CLI to exit 2 and print "traceability-maint failed:".
- tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect returns [] when no stale annotations in temp directory. - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect finds expected stale story ("stale.story.md") when referenced but file missing.
- tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] returns empty array when directory does not exist. - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detects stale annotations in nested directories with multiple non-existent story paths. - Security behavior test: ensures detectStaleAnnotations performs security validation for unsafe and invalid-extension story paths and does not call fs.existsSync on paths outside workspace or on invalid extensions; only normalized, in-workspace candidates are checked.
- tests/maintenance/update.test.ts & tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - Confirm updateAnnotationReferences returns 0 when there are no matches or when directory does not exist. - Confirm it updates a file containing `@story old.path.md` to `@story new.path.md` and returns count 1.
- tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-BATCH] batchUpdateAnnotations returns 0 when no mappings are provided. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verifyAnnotations returns true when annotations and story files are valid.
- tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] generateMaintenanceReport returns empty string when no operations/stale annotations. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] generateMaintenanceReport returns a string containing "non-existent.story.md" when file references a non-existent story.
- tests/maintenance/index.test.ts - Verifies that maintenance index exports all tools as functions, ensuring integration with overall plugin API and satisfying REQ-MAINT-SAFE for export surface.
- tests/perf/maintenance-large-workspace.test.ts - Large synthetic workspace (~500 TS files, mix of valid and stale stories): - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detectStaleAnnotations returns > 0 stale entries and completes in under 5 seconds. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verifyAnnotations returns false and runs under 5 seconds. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] generateMaintenanceReport produces non-empty output under 5 seconds. - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] updateAnnotationReferences and batchUpdateAnnotations update counts > 0 with each operation under 5 seconds. - Confirms maintainability and performance for realistic large projects, matching the story’s long-term maintainability aims.
- tests/perf/maintenance-cli-large-workspace.test.ts - CLI-level performance tests on a moderately large workspace: - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] `traceability-maint detect --root --json` returns exit code 0 or 1, runs under 5 seconds, prints JSON `{ root, stale[] }` with non-empty stale array. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] `traceability-maint report --format=json` exits 0 in under 5 seconds, outputs JSON with string `report` field. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] `traceability-maint verify --root ` exits 1, runs under 5 seconds, and prints guidance message about stale annotations.
4) Documentation and integration - README.md (Maintenance CLI section) - Describes the `traceability-maint` CLI: - Purpose: maintain and audit @story annotations across repo. - Commands: detect, verify, report, update. - Usage examples showing: - `npx traceability-maint --help` - detect/verify/report usage with --root . and --format json - update usage with --from/--to paths for renamed story files. - Directly fulfills the story’s "Documentation" acceptance criterion with practical usage and mapping to real workflows.
- docs/decisions/adr-maintenance-cli-interface.md - ADR explicitly linked to Story 009.0; documents CLI design, command semantics, exit codes, safety and error handling strategy, tests, and reasons. - Confirms alignment with story’s Technical Considerations and User Experience requirements.
- docs/maintenance-performance-tests.md - Story-tagged (**Story:** docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md). - Describes critical workflows (detection, verification/reporting, update, CLI entrypoints), scale of test workspaces, when to run performance tests, and how to interpret results. - Provides best practices for safe, scalable use of maintenance tools on large projects.
Overall, code, tests, CLI integration, and documentation all explicitly reference this story and its REQ-MAINT-* requirements. All related tests pass in the current test run, and there is no evidence of missing acceptance-criteria behavior.
traceability.notes:
Story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md is fully implemented.
Every requirement is covered by concrete implementation and tests: - REQ-MAINT-DETECT: detectStaleAnnotations and CLI detect subcommand identify stale @story references, including large-workspace and security/unsafe-path edge cases. - REQ-MAINT-UPDATE: updateAnnotationReferences (plus batchUpdateAnnotations and CLI update) safely rewrite @story paths when story files move/are renamed, with counts and dry-run support. - REQ-MAINT-BATCH: batchUpdateAnnotations performs batch updates; verified by unit and performance tests. - REQ-MAINT-VERIFY: verifyAnnotations and CLI verify check for remaining stale annotations and use explicit exit codes. - REQ-MAINT-REPORT: generateMaintenanceReport and CLI report provide human-readable and JSON summaries of stale annotations. - REQ-MAINT-SAFE: Directory existence checks, boundary enforcement, safe handling of unsafe paths, dry-run mode, clear exit codes (0/1/2), help output, and robust error handling are implemented and tested, including simulated permission errors.
Acceptance criteria are satisfied: - Core Functionality: Detection and update tools (plus batch, verify, report, and CLI) operate over real and synthetic codebases and detect/update stale references. - Quality Standards: Updates preserve code functionality and formatting by only replacing @story paths and using conditional writes; dry-run prevents unintended changes. - Integration: Maintenance helpers live in src/maintenance, are exported via src/maintenance/index.ts, exposed as a CLI bin, and reuse existing annotation/file-validation utilities. - User Experience: CLI offers clear commands, help text, messages, JSON output, and meaningful exit codes; tests assert on these behaviors. - Error Handling: Non-existent roots, invalid flags, missing parameters, unsafe paths, and permission errors are all handled gracefully with diagnostics and appropriate exit codes. - Documentation: README, ADR, and dedicated maintenance-performance documentation describe usage, options, workflows, and performance expectations.
All related Jest tests pass (npm test -- --verbose), so the story is currently in a passing, verified state.
